model: Phase61A A0 with one paragraph-line0 entry mixture; global strength fixed at 1.5 for this first joint diagnostic; no new repair mechanism added.
decision: A0 passes the narrow Phase61A entry-direction gate but fails when multiple constraints are inspected together. It trivially inherits high global edit1 type density from the empirical Voynich token inventory, yet produces only ~6.7% of Voynich local-prev10 near-family activation, overstates line-position dependence by roughly 3.3x on the mean eta2 proxy, and overshoots the multivariate entry-vs-pseudo norm by ~2.8x at the fixed strength.
important_caveat: The edit1-type result is not an independent success because A0 samples from an empirical Voynich vocabulary. The present body generator was deliberately simple; repairing local family activation would require adding an explicit local-copy/family-state mechanism, which is exactly the complexity accounting Phase61 is designed to expose.
hypothesis_update: A0 as frozen is rejected as a joint model. A boundary-aware meaningless generator remains viable only as a more complex A1 that combines at least boundary-conditioned entry mixture with a separate local token-family activation mechanism and must then be retested against line-position and section constraints.
